newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia CPI leaves activity data to decide rates.
newsitem.headline: Australia CPI leaves activity data to decide rates.

text.p: Australia's low inflation performance looks secure, but analysts doubt whether it is enough to justify a cut in interest rates as signs emerge of improving activity and rising U.S. rates.
Instead, most saw rates as on hold, despite there being a possible window of opportunity for a cut in the next six months.

Wednesday's March quarter consumer price index (CPI) data showed a rise of just 0.2 percent, leaving annual inflation at 1.3 percent. This was the lowest level in four years, a period which has also seen uninterrupted economic growth.

"In concert with the wage decision yesterday, I think it underlines the fact that the inflation picture is pretty good in Australia and likely to remain that way for a while," SBC Warburg senior economist Guy Bruten said of the data.
"We're still some way away from the inflation fundamentals deteriorating," he said.

However, analysts said as the outcome had been widely expected, activity data would determined the next move in rates. If the RBA was to move in the next three to six months, it would be to cut rates, economists said. Beyond that, a tightening remained the most likely next action.
